claims.claim: Quintus Septimius Florens Tertullianus was a Carthaginian Christian writer born around 155–160 AD and died after 220 AD.
Tertullian served as a presbyter (priest) in the church at Carthage.
He was trained as a lawyer and was familiar with Roman legal procedure.
The work "To Scapula" was addressed to Scapula, the Roman proconsul of Africa (Carthage).
It was likely composed around AD 212–217, after the death of Severus (c. 198) and after the “dark day of Utica” (c. 210).
Tertullian wrote the tract to protest the persecution of Christians that Scapula had begun to enforce and to warn him of the fate of previous persecutors.
The letter emphasizes Christian love for enemies and loyalty to the emperor while urging tolerance of the Christian community.

The work survives in the Latin original and in early English translations, notably in the Ante‑Nicene Fathers, vol. III, and in modern digital editions such as the Christian Classics Ethereal Library.
Scholars consider "To Scapula" valuable for its indices of early third‑century North‑African Christianity and its insight into the relationship between Christians and Roman officials.
The tract, written late in Tertullian’s life, contains no trace of Montanism, showing his alignment with the broader Christian community.
